name: yeule
label: Ninja Tune
lede: A Singapore teenager took a name from a Final Fantasy character, hid behind it online, and ended up with a Best New Music score for a fuzzy album about looking after your younger self.

eras.title: A name from a video game
eras.text: yeule starts as a teenager's online persona in Singapore, piles up EPs, then lands a debut album while studying art in London. The sound is dream pop, built in a bedroom.

years.cap: Early yeule artwork. Credit to be supplied.
years.h: A Final Fantasy character lends yeule a name
years.p: Nat Ćmiel releases a self-titled EP on March 3, 2014, under a stage name taken from Paddra Nsu-Yeul of Final Fantasy XIII-2.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the name comes from Paddra Nsu-Yeul, a character in Final Fantasy XIII-2, and that Ćmiel links it to accepting mortality. It also lists a jazz ensemble called Riot Diet before the solo project, and Final Fantasy and Kingdom Hearts soundtracks among the first sounds that stuck.

The project began around 2012, when Ćmiel was 14. In a FADER interview they said the online personas were freeing because you don't get trapped in one body.

years.p: Three releases in ten months: the Pathos EP (December 11, 2016), the Lost Memories Dot Net OST (July 17, 2017) and the Coma EP (September 27, 2017).
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that Duncan Cooper of The FADER called Coma dream-pop perfection. Pathos was self-released, and Coma came out on Zoom Lens.

years.p: The label releases the first two albums, Serotonin II and Glitch Princess.

years.h: Serotonin II: the debut, dreamy and digital
years.p: The first album gets a 4/5 from Tiny Mix Tapes, which praised its sound design. yeule is studying at Central Saint Martins at the time.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Ćmiel applied to Central Saint Martins for fashion communication and womenswear, and graduated in 2020 with a Fine Arts degree. The debut was made in the middle of that.

eras.title: Glitch Princess
eras.text: The persona gets a body, a face and a cyber-gothic look. yeule turns the pop up, brings in producers, and lands on Pitchfork's Best New Music list.

years.h: First single under her own name: My Name Is Nat Ćmiel
years.p: The single drops at the end of 2020 and opens the campaign for the second album.

years.h: Glitch Princess runs 327 minutes with one track
years.p: A four-hour ambient piece, "The Things They Did for Me Out of Love", stretches the digital edition. Pitchfork gave the album 8.3 and Best New Music.
years.xp:
[[Danny L Harle|1fd94d42-5e6a-46f2-84bf-9cc0be6c009f]] produced five tracks, [[Mura Masa|d2a76e1b-cecc-4500-b445-d55591821cd3]] co-produced one, and the Japanese artist [[Tohji|8d76fa36-1f77-4105-b67e-02b596024dac]] appears on another. It came out on Bayonet with a Metacritic score of 85, according to Wikipedia; Clash and The Line of Best Fit each gave it 9/10.

yeule described the shift to The FADER as a move from natural earthy gothic to a neo-technical, cyber-gothic look, with posthumanist ideas about AI and identity behind it.

years.big: "You don't get trapped in one body"
q: The idea of personas have always been really freeing for me.
years.h: The persona argument, in yeule's words
years.p: yeule tells The FADER's Salvatore Maicki that personas have always felt freeing, and says she greets her PC when she gets home.
years.xp: The interview took place around the Glitch Princess release. yeule uses she/they pronouns and identifies mainly as non-binary, according to the same piece.

eras.title: Softscars
eras.text: A new label, a heavier sound, and an album built from old journal entries called scars. Guitars come to the front and the reviews get better.

years.cap: sulky baby era press image. Credit to be supplied.
years.h: sulky baby: a new single and a Ninja Tune deal on the same day
years.p: yeule announces the Ninja Tune signing with the first new music since "Too Dead Inside", plus autumn shows in Chicago, New York, Los Angeles and London.
years.xp:
DIY reported that the song grew out of old journals yeule calls scars, read aloud to generate material. yeule called it "a 2000s alt-rock shoegaze hybrid tinted in sad satire".

The song came from talking to an earlier version of themself, in yeule's words: "stopping her from crying."

years.h: dazies and fish in the pool arrive together
years.p: Two more singles precede the album. Ghosts follows on August 9, Inferno on August 31 and the title track "softscars" on September 14.

years.src: Wikipedia: Softscars · Album of the Year · Slant Magazine
years.h: Softscars: Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and ranked it No. 10 of 2023
years.p: The third album is a Best New Music pick from Pitchfork, whose reviewer Ryan Dombal scored it 8.5 and later placed it 10th on the site's best of 2023.
years.xp:
Producers are yeule, [[Kin Leonn|11ed3790-f2a5-48fc-9a48-52c1f59cbab0]], [[Mura Masa|d2a76e1b-cecc-4500-b445-d55591821cd3]] and Chris Greatti. Wikipedia lists a Metacritic score of 83, with The Line of Best Fit at 8/10 and PopMatters at 7/10. Stereogum named it Album of the Week.

Slant's Eric Mason wrote that yeule "expands, refines, and masters their creative vision". Physical copies followed on October 6.

eras.title: Heavier still
eras.text: yeule pushes further into 90s and 2000s alt-rock and metal. The reviews split.

years.src: Wikipedia: Evangelic Girl Is a Gun
years.h: Eko is the first song from album four
years.p: The single lands in late October 2024, months before the album gets a title.

years.src: Wikipedia: Evangelic Girl Is a Gun · Wikipedia: Yeule
years.h: Skullcrusher is co-produced with Clams Casino and Fitnesss
years.p: yeule announces the fourth album the same day as the second single.
years.xp: [[Clams Casino|772a0eb3-fe31-4a08-b583-690296f44900]] and [[A.G. Cook|b12ef43e-72ad-43d0-b216-a8cd32f78852]] are among the producers on the album, along with Ćmiel, Fitnesss, Chris Greatti, Kin Leonn and Mura Masa, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Evangelic Girl Is a Gun
years.h: Evangelic Girl Is a Gun: Pitchfork gives it 5.9
years.p: A 31-minute album citing painter Zdzislaw Beksinski. Clash gave it 9/10 and Metacritic lists 81 from ten critics.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the record as leaving the glitchy dream pop of Softscars for shoegaze, grunge and 90s alternative, with themes of self-destruction and literary romanticism. It reached No. 18 on the UK Independent Albums chart and No. 29 in Scotland.
